add: versionless
A file version with `versioning` 1 (2 in the search index), whose content the purge deletes once a newer version commits.
VersioningRules, RepoVersioning
A network's signed path rules, or a repo's own replacing them, that set each new path's versioning; absent both, paths over 64 MiB are versionless.
git-lfs store
A repo's versionless `ur/lfs` ref of git-lfs objects, moved through the daemon with no LFS server and pruned after 30 unreferenced days.
search index
A repo's encrypted, versionless trigram index, updated by every committer and downloaded whole to search locally, so evs never sees a query.
bucket (search index)
An index partition of W days' entries, 30 by default, of which every syncing device keeps the newest two.
all partition
The index's older documents, one version each, rolled up from expired buckets; desktops and indexers keep it, others fetch on demand.
roll-up
Merging an expired bucket into the all partition and removing it in one locked push, by a search indexer, else the first writer after expiry.
verified hit, possible match
A hit checked against the document's text, and a trigram candidate shown from display fields, unchecked until opened.
.ur-index/, ur/index
The search index's roots: `.ur-index/` inside each file-mode ref, committed with its documents, and a repo's `ur/index` ref for git-mode refs and streams.
companion push
A committer's later push of its git-mode refs' and streams' index entries to `ur/index`, within one to five minutes.
IndexSettings
A repo admin's versioned file in each index root that turns the index off or sets its bucket window.
indexer
An always-on device its network designates by IndexerSet, none by default, to run background services (mail, mirrors, search upkeep) first, gaining no access.
IndexerSet
The config statement designating an indexer and its sealed services (mail, mirror, search), at network or member scope.
mail indexer
A receiver its network designates for mail by IndexerSet, through which alone a network receives reliably.
team directory
A team network's one repo of kind `directory`, read by every admitted sidecar, holding announcements, access requests and the coordination log.
announcement
A team-directory item stating who, what and where for a run, worker or repo; runs and workers expire unless renewed.
card (directory)
A sidecar's signed DirectoryCard in the team directory, holding up to 16 of its run and worker announcements.
notice (directory)
A small directory file under `q/<target>/` flagging an access request to its target's approvers, rewritten once decided.
directory stub
How tools return directory announcements, requests and decisions by default: attested and identifier fields and the match label, no prose.
private marker
A private repo's directory file: its signer, id, kind and request state only, padded like an announcement.
remote search
An app host's "search more" sent end to end to a designated search indexer, which answers with verified hits in fixed-size replies.
drop (DROP push), drop pending, dropped
A repo admin's push deleting the content only a path's earlier versions name; they read drop pending, cancellable, for 7 days (none with --now), then dropped, statements and hashes kept.
autogroup:dst-owner
The approver atom for a grant's destination subject's owner or, for a tagged sidecar, its sponsor, else an admin.
claims (setting)
A member's per-project setting for announcing runs: auto at start (the team default), prompt at a claim, or off.
format 2
v1's storage format (versionless content, history drops, the search index, git-lfs), which a repo adopts without rewriting at its first push under the `format2` gate.
coordination log
Where claims, handoffs, asks, answers, checks and notes go: the team directory in a team network, else the member's vault.

receiver: A sidecar listening on `smtp/25/mx` that terminates inbound mail TLS and deposits messages, reliably only as a designated mail indexer.
direct MX: A Team option pointing MX straight at up to two of its mail indexers, bypassing mxedge.
record repo: A `record`-kind ledger with grantee readers and append-only owned refs, never the coordination log.
repo kind: A repo's fixed type: general, record, config, directory, team_record, mailcfg, vault, mailbox or secret.
leaves rule: A network's first 1,000 live member devices are its config and team directory groups' leaves; later ones read by wraps, committing no Add or Remove.
readers(repo): The sidecars policy lets read a repo: member devices as its MLS leaves, others, config and directory overflow included, through wraps.
RECORD.md: The separate design of recURd's record semantics, an M0 deliverable.
`.ur` file: A committable project file naming the default network and, optionally, the `claims` setting and `project` label.
hold (preservation): A legal hold pausing only the server's TTL sweeps, GC and history drops for in-scope objects, never users' shredding.
fault schedule (FS-n): A deterministic script of actor steps, barriers, store faults and clock moves, checked against FI-1 to FI-27.
index entry: A path's `idx/` object in evs's path index, one per path epoch, holding folded committed versions.
remote mode: An sdk backend driving a desktop `ur daemon` instead of a local sidecar (not remote search's on/own/off).
engine: Service logic in the sidecar repo behind host interfaces, hosted by server, unlike the devices' search engine.
coverage: The record's statement of which hooks observed a run, and any lapse; not search coverage.
